decisions.reason: The premium raisin stollen is the firm's publicly announced flagship and has repeatedly won the Deutsches Brotinstitut gold medal, so commitment and proven success both argue for keeping it.

The dark barley malt rye shows no reported success and the firm already pruned similar rye variants, but it runs on existing know-how and facilities at little added cost and still has its own page, so management keeps it a while longer.
The marzipan stollen rounds out the flagship Christmas stollen line in the seasonal gift business, so dropping it would weaken the firm's committed holiday direction.
The ancient grain bread was publicly announced as the firm's newest masterpiece, and weak early results can still be attributed to the time needed to build demand, so management keeps backing it.
